# Tokamak The tokamak is a fusion engine. A magnetic field holds a cloud of plasma inside the core while gyrotrons heat it and injectors feed it fuel. The hotter the plasma, the more power the core puts onto the high voltage network.
## Setting it up Place the core and connect its HV cable to the grid. The core, gyrotrons, injectors and harvesters all need ordinary APC power as well.
Gyrotrons and injectors fire in a straight line, so each one has to face the core with a clear row or column between them. The console shows whether each device is aligned. The console must be within 40 tiles of the core.
## Running it - Load a fuel rod into each injector and turn everything on from the console. - Gyrotrons heat the plasma. Fuel only reacts once the plasma is hot enough for that particular reaction. - Raising the field strength lets the core hold more, but draws more power and makes the plasma less stable. - People standing next to the core disturb the field. Keep the area clear. - Helium ash builds up as fuel burns and crowds the plasma. Keep an eye on instability.
If instability reaches 100% the field ruptures: the core explodes, irradiates the area and sends out an EMP. The console has a SCRAM button that dumps the field safely, but it still releases some radiation.
## Fuels Deuterium and tritium ignite first and are the easiest way to get going. Lithium and deuterium breed more tritium. Deuterium and helium-3 burn cleanly, and hydrogen and boron burn hot enough to need a careful hand.
Hot enough plasma can also transmute iron into silver and silver into gold. Place a harvester within a few tiles of the core to press them into ingots. This is extremely unstable.
